title: Africa 7 of 8 · Southern Africa
edition: Africa countries · Eight regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to Africa episode seven of eight. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
Our longest lesson covers ten countries across southern Africa, from Angola to Eswatini. Follow the coasts, the Zambezi neighbours and the two small countries beside South Africa.

states.name: Angola
lines: Angola faces the Atlantic below the Democratic Republic of the Congo and above Namibia. Zambia lies east, while Cabinda is a separate northern coastal exclave.
Mbanza Kongo preserves the former capital of the kingdom of Kongo. Its remains record an African political centre and the changes that followed contact with Portuguese traders and Christianity.
Picture an old royal capital on the Atlantic side of southern Africa. Angola is above Namibia; remember that Cabinda is separated from its main territory.
states.transition: Let's bring Angola and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Zambia
lines: Zambia is landlocked east of Angola, below the Democratic Republic of the Congo and above Zimbabwe. Malawi and Mozambique lie toward its east.
At Mosi-oa-Tunya, also called Victoria Falls, the Zambezi drops into basalt gorges and throws up clouds of spray. The falls are shared with Zimbabwe across the river.
Picture falling water on the southern border. Zambia is above Zimbabwe; their shared waterfall helps keep the pair in the right order.
states.transition: Let's bring Zambia and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Malawi
lines: Malawi is the narrow inland country east of Zambia and west and north of Mozambique. Lake Malawi follows much of its eastern side, below Tanzania.
Lake Malawi National Park is famous for its diversity of fish, including many species found nowhere else. These related fish provide an important window into evolution.
Picture colourful fish along a long lake. Malawi is the slim inland country; Mozambique curves around its southern and eastern sides.

states.name: Mozambique
lines: Mozambique stretches along the Indian Ocean below Tanzania and east of Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe. South Africa and Eswatini lie toward its southern end.
The Island of Mozambique preserves buildings shaped by African, Arab and European connections across the Indian Ocean. Its town records a long history of maritime exchange.
Remember a historic trading island beside the long eastern coast. Mozambique is on the ocean; Malawi and Zambia behind it are landlocked.

states.name: Zimbabwe
lines: Zimbabwe is landlocked below Zambia, west of Mozambique and above South Africa. Botswana lies toward its southwest.

Great Zimbabwe preserves the remains of an important medieval trading city associated with Shona civilisation. Its imposing stone enclosures challenge the idea that African urban history began with European colonisation.
Picture a stone city below Zambia. Zimbabwe sits between the Zambezi region and South Africa, with Mozambique separating it from the Indian Ocean.

states.name: Botswana
lines: Botswana is landlocked above South Africa, east of Namibia and southwest of Zimbabwe. A very short northern boundary reaches Zambia.
The Okavango Delta spreads inland instead of flowing to the sea. Floodwater arrives in the dry season, supporting wetlands and wildlife amid a much drier surrounding region.
Picture a river opening into an inland wetland. Botswana has a delta but no coastline; Namibia lies between it and the Atlantic.
states.transition: Let's bring Botswana and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Namibia
lines: Namibia follows the Atlantic below Angola and west of Botswana. South Africa lies south, while its narrow northeastern extension reaches toward the Zambezi.
In the Namib Sand Sea, coastal fog supplies water to a desert dune ecosystem. Animals and plants survive using moisture that comes from the ocean air rather than regular rainfall.
Picture fog drifting over dunes beside the Atlantic. Namibia is the western coastal country; Botswana is inland to its east.

states.name: South Africa
lines: South Africa occupies the continent’s southern end, facing both the Atlantic and Indian Oceans. Namibia, Botswana and Zimbabwe lie north; Lesotho is completely enclosed within it.

Mapungubwe preserves the remains of a medieval kingdom near the meeting of the Limpopo and Shashe rivers. Southern Africa had important political centres and trading networks long before modern borders.
Picture an old kingdom at the northern edge of the southernmost country. Keep Lesotho inside South Africa, and Eswatini beside its eastern side.

states.name: Lesotho
lines: Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa. It occupies a mountainous inland area, with no border to any other country and no coast.
The Maloti-Drakensberg landscape combines high mountain habitats with rock art made by San people. The paintings preserve a cultural record within a dramatic mountain setting.
Picture a mountain island on land, enclosed by South Africa. Lesotho is the fully surrounded country; Eswatini also borders Mozambique.
states.transition: Let's bring Lesotho and its neighbours into view.

states.name: Eswatini
lines: Eswatini is the small country between eastern South Africa and Mozambique. It is landlocked, even though the Indian Ocean lies relatively nearby.
Eswatini was previously known internationally as Swaziland. The country’s present name makes a useful reminder to match modern naming with the same small geographic location.
Keep the two small southern countries apart. Eswatini touches Mozambique; Lesotho is entirely surrounded by South Africa. Neither has an ocean coast.
states.transition: Let's bring Eswatini and its neighbours into view.

recap: Angola and Namibia follow the Atlantic. Zambia lies above Zimbabwe; Malawi is beside its long lake, and Mozambique follows the Indian Ocean coast. Botswana is inland between Namibia, Zimbabwe and South Africa.

South Africa occupies the southern end. Lesotho is entirely enclosed inside it; Eswatini also touches Mozambique. Remember the royal capital, waterfall, lake fish, maritime island, stone city, inland delta, fog dunes and highland rock art.
